run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T10:29:06Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by a real but small, sustained stream of ERROR-status spans on the frontend-proxy 'ingress' server span: the one-hour increase of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",span_name="ingress",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} was 25.26 -> 31.48 across the authorized window, against 19,058.84 -> 22,490 spans of the same operation, i.e. about 0.1% of ingress spans (5-minute ratio 0.00113 at 10:29:06; per-operation 5-minute error rate 0.0111 errors/s). The error counter climbed monotonically (1082 at 10:02:43 to 1113 at 10:36:43) with no step, and the 1-minute ERROR rate at the exact alert instant was 0, so this is a low-level continuous trickle rather than a spike. frontend-proxy looks healthy at pod and workload level (Running, Ready, restartCount 0 since 09:49:10Z, ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-6b4d584985 1/1 ready owned by deployment frontend-proxy), its 'router frontend egress' client spans show zero ERROR increase, no other otel-demo service except recommendation (4.06/h), ad (2.04/h) and fraud-detection (2.04/h) shows any ERROR-span increase, all ingress spans completed under about 5s, and every fault-injection feature flag in flagd-config is left at its "off" default. What remains unresolved is which requests produce those ERROR spans: the queried Prometheus loads no alert rules and its 63-name inventory has no HTTP, RPC or kube-state metric families, the trace store only reaches about 10:02 and the sampled spans carry 200 or 308 statuses only, and the proxy access logs were readable only for about 6 seconds (10:20:02-10:20:08), where only 200 and 308 responses appear.

claims.text: For service_name="frontend-proxy" the only ERROR-status span metrics are on span_name="ingress" (SPAN_KIND_SERVER) and span_name="router frontend egress" (SPAN_KIND_CLIENT), both emitted by the single otel-collector pod otel-collector-564d9c7987-6j4x2.

Whole-window one-hour increases for frontend-proxy: ingress ERROR rose 25.26 -> 31.48 spans, ingress STATUS_CODE_UNSET rose 19058.84 -> 22490, while 'router frontend egress' ERROR stayed exactly 0 at every step.

At the alert instant 2026-11-15T10:29:06Z the frontend-proxy error ratio was 0.000566 over all spans, and per operation the 'ingress' ratio was 0.00113 while 'router frontend egress' was 0; the 5-minute error rate by operation was 0.0111 errors/s for ingress and 0 for egress.

The frontend-proxy ERROR counter was 1082 at 10:02:43 and 1113 at 10:36:43 (31 error spans in about 34 minutes) and increased monotonically; the 5-minute ingress error rate sampled every 2 minutes ranged only 0.0037 to 0.037 errors/s (about 1 to 10 error spans per 5-minute window) with no step increase.
At the exact alert instant the 1-minute ERROR rate for frontend-proxy was 0, so no error burst occurred in the minute before the alert's own timestamp.

Across all services only four had a nonzero ERROR-span increase in the window: frontend-proxy 31.48/h, recommendation 4.06/h, ad 2.04/h and fraud-detection 2.04/h; frontend, cart, checkout, product-catalog, payment, shipping, currency, email, accounting, quote, image-provider and kafka showed no ERROR spans.
The ad and fraud-detection error ratios of 1.0 are confined to span_name flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream (long-lived flagd event-stream spans), not to request-serving operations.

All frontend-proxy ingress spans are fast: the whole-window increase of traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket for span_name="ingress" reaches 22514.38 at le=2000 and 22521.48 at le=5000 and +Inf, i.e. only about 7 ingress spans in the window exceeded 2s and none exceeded 5s.

Kubernetes state: all 21 otel-demo pods are Running and Ready; frontend-proxy pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-p6mgt has restartCount 0 and startTime 2026-11-15T09:49:10Z, and fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-wvrwx is the only pod with a restart (restartCount 1).

ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-6b4d584985 is owned by deployment frontend-proxy, was created 2026-11-15T09:49:09Z and has 1/1 ready replicas (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend-proxy); all other otel-demo ReplicaSets were also created 09:49:09-09:51:03Z, consistent with one environment-wide rollout before the alert.

The newest readable frontend-proxy Envoy access-log lines (13,652 lines read, covering 2026-11-15T10:20:02Z to 10:20:08Z) contain only HTTP 200 and 308 responses (for example "GET /api/products/... 200" and "GET /api/data/?contextKeys=... 308").

The trace sample kept for frontend-proxy (about 10:01:57-10:02:01, 640 spans) shows ingress and 'router frontend egress' spans with http.status_code 200 and 308 only; no row in the reviewed slices (offsets 0, 60, 100) carries an error status tag or error detail.

Jaeger tag search did return frontend-proxy traces for http.status_code="200" (2 traces, 18 spans, all with http.status_code 200 on ingress/egress) and for http.status_code="308" (1 trace, 13 spans, ingress and egress with http.status_code 308 alongside a 200), which confirms 200 and 308 are the codes present in the stored frontend-proxy trace sample.

The queried Prometheus exposes 63 metric names; the only trace-derived families are traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket, and no http_server_request_duration_seconds_count, rpc_* or kube-state-metrics names appear in that inventory.
status_code label values present on traces_span_metrics_calls_total are STATUS_CODE_ERROR, STATUS_CODE_OK and STATUS_CODE_UNSET.

The flagd-config ConfigMap (key demo.flagd.json) defines adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure, and every one of them has defaultVariant "off".

The alert's value 0.0333 is best read as an error rate in errors/second over a 5-minute range: 9 errors / 270 s = 0.0333, which matches the observed magnitude of the signal (the 5-minute ingress error rate ranged 0.0037-0.037 errors/s, i.e. 1-10 error spans per 5 minutes). On that reading the alert fired because the small but persistent ERROR-span trickle for frontend-proxy exceeded a '> 0' threshold, not because of a sudden degradation.

The ERROR status on frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans is produced by responses that do not appear as HTTP 4xx/5xx in the stored trace sample: the sampled spans show 200 and 308 only, the egress client span is never error-marked, and no downstream service records ERROR spans, so the failing responses are either proxy-local replies or error-status spans whose HTTP code tag is absent from the sampled data. The concrete failing requests and routes remain unidentified.

frontend-proxy shows no infrastructure failure: its pod is Running/Ready with restartCount 0 since 09:49:10Z, its ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-6b4d584985 is 1/1 ready under deployment frontend-proxy, and the container has no previous instance to read.

No downstream service's own error signal accompanies the frontend-proxy ingress errors: frontend, cart, checkout, product-catalog, payment, shipping, currency, email, accounting, quote, image-provider and kafka all show zero ERROR-span increase in the window, and the frontend's server spans in the reviewed traces are HTTP 200.

Slow requests exist but are not errors: traces filtered to frontend-proxy ingress spans longer than 2s (up to 2.48s, for user_get_recommendations and user_add_to_cart transactions) all carry http.status_code 200 on ingress, egress, frontend and downstream spans.

Fault injection through the demo feature flags is not the cause: every relevant flag (cartFailure, paymentFailure, productCatalogFailure, adFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems and the others) has defaultVariant "off" in the flagd-config ConfigMap, and no cart, checkout, payment or product-catalog ERROR spans were observed.

A crash, OOM or readiness failure of frontend-proxy is not the cause: restartCount is 0, the container has no previous instance, the pod has been Ready since 09:49:10Z, and all 21 otel-demo pods are Running and Ready.

Advisory only, not executed: read the RequestErrorRate rule expression, range, denominator and threshold in the alerting Prometheus, and if the rule triggers on any nonzero rate for a service that carries a continuous ~1-4 errors/minute trickle at about 0.1% of ingress spans, review whether a '> 0' condition over a short range fits the intended signal.

Advisory only, not executed: export frontend-proxy (Envoy) access logs for the minutes around 2026-11-15T10:29:06Z including response codes and response flags, since only about 6 seconds of log were readable here, to identify the exact statuses behind the ERROR ingress spans.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alert rule is not present in the queried Prometheus: the rule queries for rule_name=RequestErrorRate, for {severity="warning"} and unfiltered each returned no_data (no rules), so the expression, range, denominator and threshold behind the reported value 0.0333 are unverified.

Retention limits the baseline: traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy"} samples begin at 10:02:43 (the 24h query's source starts about 10:06:43), so no pre-incident or multi-day baseline exists and no earlier change in error rate can be assessed.

The Jaeger store only reaches about 10:00-10:02 for these queries, so the ERROR spans themselves were never sampled; tag searches for error=true, otel.status_code="ERROR" and http.status_code 500/502/503/504/400/404/429/499 returned no_data (no matching trace), and frontend/load-generator span searches for 500/404 also returned no_data, so the failing status codes remain unknown and codes not tried are not excluded.
The frontend container emitted no readable log lines at all in the window (two fetch attempts, with and without a filter, read 0 lines), so frontend application-level errors could not be checked.
frontend-proxy access logs were readable only for the newest about 4 MiB (roughly 6 s, 10:20:02-10:20:08); no 5xx appeared there, but that window is far too small to characterize the error responses.

Kubernetes events for frontend/frontend-proxy returned no_data in the window; expired events cannot be distinguished from events that never existed, so no event-level confirmation of a restart or eviction is available.

The change_history integration is not integrated, so deployment, configuration and flag-change history for the window (including the flagd ReplicaSet change at 09:51:03 and the fraud-detection restart) is unavailable.

flagd runtime flag values during the window were not verified; only the ConfigMap defaults were read, so an out-of-band override through flagd-ui cannot be excluded and ConfigMap contents cannot prove runtime state.
Whether the ERROR spans correspond to requests a customer would see as failures is unverified; no non-2xx span was observed from the load-generator either.

The queried Prometheus has no kube-state-metrics families (no kube_pod_owner or kube_deployment_status_* in its 63-name inventory), so deployment-level replica/availability metrics were unavailable; Kubernetes object state used instead reflects only the moment of the query.

The spans at offset 0, 60 and 100 of the stored frontend-proxy trace result are slices of an incomplete and truncated view (610+ rows unread), so absence of error tags there does not cover the whole sample.
next_steps: Read the RequestErrorRate alert rule expression and threshold in the alerting Prometheus or Alertmanager rule source to confirm what 0.0333 measures and over which range.

Export frontend-proxy (Envoy) access logs with response codes and response flags for the minutes around 2026-11-15T10:29:06Z, beyond the ~6 s that was readable, to identify the exact statuses behind the ERROR ingress spans.
Check flagd runtime flag values and flagd-ui override history for the incident window to rule out an applied failure injection that ConfigMap defaults do not show.
If noise reduction is the goal, review whether a zero-tolerance error-rate condition suits a service whose only error signal is a steady ~1-4 errors/minute (advisory only, not executed).
